A_target.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite [[Definition:Connected Graph|connected]] [[Definition:Multigraph|multigraph]] with at least one edge.
Then $G$ has an [[Definition:Eulerian Circuit|Eulerian circuit]] {{iff}} every vertex has [[Definition:Even Integer|even]] [[Definition:Degree of Vertex|degree]].

B_source.statement: Every finite multigraph in which every vertex has degree at least $2$ contains a [[Definition:Cycle (Graph Theory)|cycle]].

substitutions.the graph with minimum degree 2: the non-isolated part of an even graph

derived.repeatedly extracted cycles: pieces spliced into one closed trail

object_map.reformulation: Remove a cycle, apply induction to what remains, and splice the resulting circuits into the cycle.

validity_conditions: Removing the edges of a cycle keeps all degrees even.
Connectedness ensures that every remaining component meets the removed cycle.
proof_plan: An Eulerian circuit enters and leaves each vertex the same number of times, so every degree is even.

Conversely, proceed by induction on the number of edges.
The non-isolated vertices all have even degree, hence degree at least $2$, so by the source result there is a cycle $C$.

Removing the edges of $C$ leaves all degrees even.
By the induction hypothesis, each component of the remainder with an edge has an Eulerian circuit.
